pass_a_gloss: With whole soul I consider God to be loved by those drawing off and standing apart the soul, through much eagerness toward sharing with God, not only from the earthy body but also from every body; for whom not even with distraction and some pulling around happens the putting away of the body of lowliness, when occasion gives through the supposed death to put off the body of death and to be listened to, having prayed apostolically and having said: miserable I a human; who will rescue me out of the body of this death? For who of those groaning in the tent through being weighed by the corruptible body will not also give thanks, having said earlier: who will rescue me out of the body of this death? seeing that through the companionship having been rescued from the body of the death he will holily sound out the: grace to God through Christ Jesus our Lord.
pass_b_english: God is loved with the whole soul, I think, by those who, in their great eagerness for communion with God, draw the soul away and set it apart not only from the earthly body but from every body. For them, laying aside “the body of humiliation” (Philippians 3:21) comes about without any distraction or being dragged this way and that, whenever the moment allows them, through what is thought to be death, to strip off the body “of death”, and to be heard when they have prayed as the apostle did and said, “Wretched man that I am! Who will rescue me from the body of this death?” (Romans 7:24).

For who among those who groan “in the tent” (2 Corinthians 5:4) because they are weighed down by the perishable body (Wisdom of Solomon 9:15) will not also give thanks, after first saying, “Who will rescue me from the body of this death?”, when he sees that, rescued through this converse [with God] from “the body of death”, he will in holiness cry out, “Thanks be to God through Christ Jesus our Lord” (Romans 7:25)?

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. II); the old English was a digest; it misread τοῦ γηΐνου σώματος as a 'corpse' of a body, ran the thanksgiving question into a statement, and tacked on the start of chapter III (the Psalm 42 passage).
Checked against the Patristic Text Archive digitisation of Koetschau (pta0007.pta007.pta-grc1), which reads γηΐνου, “earthly”; rendered “the earthly body”.

Read ἀποσπώντων καὶ διϊστάντων, κοινωνῆσαι, τὸ τῆς ταπεινώσεως σῶμα (OCR „ro“ „eng ταπεινάσεως“ „ooua“), ἐκδύσασθαι (OCR ἐκδίσασθαι, confirmed by PTA), ῥύσεται / ῥυσθείς (OCR δύσεται / δυσθείς), πρότερον (OCR πρότεροι, confirmed by PTA), σκήνει, κυρίου.
“[with God]” after “this converse” (διὰ τῆς ὁμιλίας); see translator notes.

source_text: Ὅλῃ δὲ ψυχῇ νομίζω ἀγαπᾶσϑαι τὸν ϑεὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀποσπώντῶν καὶ διστάντον αὐτὴν διὰ πολλὴν τὴν πρὸς τὸ κοινονῆσαι τῷ ϑεῷ προϑυμίαν οὐ μόνον ἀπὸ τοῦ znlvov σώματος ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀπὸ παντὸς σώματος" οἷς οὐδὲ μετὰ περισπασμοῦ καὶ περιελκυσμοῦ τινος γίνεται τὸ ἀποϑέσϑαι „ro“ „eng ταπεινάσεως" „ooua“, ὅταν καιρὸς διδῷ διὰ τοῦ νομιζομένου ϑανάτου ἐκδίσασϑαι τὸ σῶμα «τοῦ ϑανάτου" καὶ ἐπαχουσϑῆναι ἀποστολιχῶς εὐξάμενον καὶ εἰπόντα .ταλαίπωρος ἐγαὺ ἀνϑρῶπος᾿ τίς με δύσεται ἐκ τοῦ σώματος τοῦ ϑανάτου τούτου" τίς γὰρ τῶν „ev τῷ σχήνει" στεναζόντων διὰ τὸ βαρεῖσϑαι ὑπὸ τοῦ φϑαρτοῦ σώματος οὐχὶ καὶ εὐχαριστήσει πρότεροι' εἰπών" „tig μὲ δύσεται ἐκ τοῦ σώματος τοῦ ϑανάτου τούτου;" βλέπων ὅτι διὰ τῆς ὁμιλίας δυσϑεὶς ἀπὸ ,τοῦ σώματος τοῦ ϑανάτου" ἁγίως ἀναφϑέγξεται τό: ,χάρις τῷ ϑεῷ διὰ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ χιρίου ἡμῶν".
